subject: Logic
title: Risk vs. Uncertainty
description: A quick win: understand Risk vs. Uncertainty.

hook.text: Rolling a die is risky—you know the odds. Starting a new business? That's uncertain.

buildup.text: Risk has known probabilities. Uncertainty means you don't even know all the possible outcomes.

discovery.text: Frank Knight defined this distinction in 1921. Insurance handles risk. Uncertainty requires judgment.

twist.text: Most real decisions involve uncertainty, not risk. Yet we treat them as if the odds are known.

climax.text: Knowing which you face changes your strategy. Risk calls for math. Uncertainty calls for flexibility.

quiz.question: What distinguishes uncertainty from risk?
options: Risk has known probabilities; uncertainty doesn't
